newsitem.title: FRANCE: Andre Courreges buys back his perfume operation.
newsitem.headline: Andre Courreges buys back his perfume operation.

text.p: Andre Courreges, one of France's few independent fashion designers, has bought back his perfume operation from a Swiss firm which acquired it in 1992, the Courreges fashion house announced on Thursday.
"We are getting back our freedom to create," Courreges spokeswoman Caroline Ryan told Reuters.
"The family now controls 100 percent of all of its activities and can make its own development choices, and the priority is on creativity," she said.

Courreges, 73, marked fashion history in the 1960s with the introduction of crisp, clean-line clothing that liberated women from girdles and high-heeled shoes. But his main claim to fame is the mini-skirt and the jumpsuit.
The fashion house said Courreges and his wife Coqueline, 61, had repurchased Courreges Parfums from the privately held Burrus Group for 38 million French francs ($7.5 million).
Burrus, a Swiss cigarette, cigar and chocolates firm, had acquired control of Courreges Parfums in 1992 from the L'Oreal Group fashion firm for an undisclosed price.
Coqueline Courreges is chairman and chief executive officer of the Courreges SA fashion house.
Courreges had launched his perfume operation in 1965 with financial help from L'Oreal, which ended up controlling the firm.
Courreges Parfum's 1995 turnover was 38.9 million francs ($7.6 million) while Courreges SA had a 1995 turnover of 125 million francs ($25 million). ($1=5.080 French Franc)
